exposure: Intrathecal recombinant human arylsulfatase A (rhASA; SHP611, now TAK-611) at doses of 10, 30, or 100 mg administered every other week
outcome: Safety and tolerability (e.g., serious adverse events)
Change in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sulfatide and lysosulfatide levels
Motor function (assessed by Gross Motor Function Measure-88 total score)
cohort: The study enrolled 24 children with Metachromatic Leukodystrophy (MLD) who experienced symptom onset aged <= 30 months.
finding: Intrathecal rhASA was generally well tolerated at doses up to 100 mg every other week, with significant reductions in CSF sulfatide and lysosulfatide levels and a tendency towards a less pronounced decline in motor function in higher dose cohorts.
